escena: SCENE (documentary photograph, a real international trade fair hall at the end of the day, NO fantasy, NO glowing effects): the sales manager from the reference portrait, wearing her own tailored charcoal-grey blazer over a plain white top, with no logo and no print anywhere, stands behind the counter of a simple exhibition stand on the RIGHT half of the frame, her face at about 70 % of the frame width and at about 38 % of the frame height, framed from the waist up, camera about two meters away at chest height, 85mm f/2. She has just finished a meeting: with her right hand she holds a current flagship smartphone with very thin bezels at chest height and types the visit into it, eyes down on the screen with a small, satisfied closed-mouth smile; between two fingers of her left hand she holds a visitor's business card, its print tiny and out of focus. She never looks at the lens. The cool white light of the phone screen is her key light: it lights her face from below and in front, the far side of her face falls into soft shadow. Far behind her on the right, out of focus, the aisle of the fair: other stands with cool white and pale blue lights melted into round bokeh, a few distant people as soft silhouettes, banners whose print is far too small and blurred to read. The whole frame is cool and contemporary: nothing warm, amber, orange or golden, no tungsten. The LEFT 45 % of the frame is the dim, calm end of the stand: a plain dark wall in shadow, no lights, no people, no objects, no text. Rich contrast, no logos of any brand, no legible text.
